nodes.label: Capability Gate / Tag System
nodes.rationale: Capabilities are OR-intersection filters (agent sees action if capabilities overlap), not AND (would require agents to hold every tag). Not a security enforcement mechanism — they filter what the brain is shown, not what can be physically executed. A brain that constructs an Intent for a gated action will fail at validate_intent() because the action won't be in the agent's visible schema set.

nodes.label: AgentOwnershipMode (BindToExisting vs CreateAtRuntime)
nodes.rationale: BindToExisting: agent declared in YAML, Unity attaches visual shell only, no RPC sent. CreateAtRuntime: Unity owns lifecycle, sends register/unregister RPCs. Phase 4 audit flags 'ownership' as a misleading name — the actual difference is who drives agent lifecycle, not who owns data (Python always owns all agent state). Proposed rename to AgentLifecycleMode.

nodes.label: AgentView Immutability Pattern
nodes.rationale: AgentRuntime never passes a mutable Agent to brains, handlers, or worlds. It wraps in AgentView — a frozen snapshot valid only for one step. Handlers that want to change inventory must return ActionResult with state_mutations; the runtime applies mutations after the handler returns. This makes mutation auditable and snapshotable, and prevents order-of-execution bugs in the simultaneous scheduler.

nodes.label: Snapshot/Restore Protocol (pickle-based)
nodes.rationale: Uses Python pickle with per-process HMAC-SHA256 signing. Known design debt: not cross-process portable, not version-stable, not inspectable. The serialize()/restore() protocol on each component already provides the right interface — the outer SimulationSnapshot container just needs to switch to a JSON/msgpack format with explicit version fields.

nodes.label: Tick Execution Sequence (Hot Path)
nodes.rationale: Per-tick: ObservationRegistry providers (lowest priority) merged with world.observe() then engine-injected fields (highest priority, always overwrite). SimultaneousScheduler dispatches all brain.decide() calls concurrently via asyncio.gather; action results applied in completion order — a known intra-tick snapshot vs. application ordering tradeoff accepted for throughput.

nodes.label: HostedWorld / ExternalWorld Pattern
nodes.rationale: World whose authoritative state is provided by an external host (Unity). Engine runs cognition; host pushes observations and receives engine_commands. Phase 4 audit notes the name 'HostedWorld' is ambiguous ('hosted' could mean hosted by the server). Protocol it implements is already named ExternalWorld; renaming the class would align the two names.

nodes.label: EventBus (Synchronous Pub/Sub)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous, not async, by design: simple, predictable, debuggable. All cross-cutting effects (social graph, logging, event streaming) go through events rather than direct coupling — this is an architectural invariant. SocialEffectSubscriber is the only mechanism to update the social graph; handlers must emit side_effects, the engine does not infer social effects.

nodes.label: WebSocket Protocol v1
nodes.rationale: JSON over WebSocket, text frames, no binary encoding. Frame types: hlo (hello), req (request), res (response), evt (event). Known debt: dual agent registration wire formats (register_agent flat params vs agent.register dot-notation) — a versioning artifact adding handler dispatch complexity. Phase 4 recommends deprecating the flat format.

nodes.label: Brain Protocol (async decide())
nodes.rationale: The Brain protocol requires a single async decide() method. Known design debt: no Brain.cleanup() hook — when an agent is unregistered, its Brain is garbage-collected with no callback to release external resources (persistent HTTP sessions, thread pools). Also: OllamaLLMBrain has no per-call timeout; if Ollama hangs indefinitely, all agents block forever on that tick.
